scope: Review of isolated Codex CLI outputs for all 130 skripsi-skill eval cases (EVAL-001...110, SUP-*, QUAL-01...12) against each oracle's expected/forbidden text, after the quality upgrade (PR #13, merged at c60a15a) and the follow-up fixes 58a9d29 and d4c8108. Raw records: live-v2/<case>.json. PASS means the observed answer met the oracle in this one scenario; it is not global requirement proof. previous_verdict refers to live-review.json (runtime d7490cd, Codex CLI 0.154.0, 118 cases).
host: Windows Codex CLI 0.166.0, CLI default model, codex exec --ignore-user-config --ephemeral, read-only sandbox with -c windows.sandbox="elevated", no network or connectors, oracle hidden from the model. Skill copied from the recorded git revision (skills/skripsi-skill subtree) into a temporary directory per case.

verdict_scale.PASS: Expected behaviour present and nothing forbidden.
verdict_scale.PARTIAL: Core expected behaviour present and nothing forbidden, but a required element of the expected text is missing.
verdict_scale.FAIL: Forbidden behaviour present or the core expected behaviour absent.

contamination: Codex discovers globally installed skills even with --ignore-user-config. Before the first ai-rules setup of the new skill (2026-11-23T19:56:59Z) four records (EVAL-005, 015, 018, 026) read the OLD skill at ~/.agents/skills/skripsi-skill; they were deleted and re-run at c60a15a after setup. The other 27 records started before that setup did not read ~/.agents. Twelve records (EVAL-040, 042, 052, 064, 065, 087, 092, 096, QUAL-01, QUAL-07, QUAL-10, SUP-ACTION-BOUNDARY) read ~/.agents after setup, when it held the same skill bytes as the revision under test. Before each later re-run batch, setup was repeated for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Antigravity CLI and diff -rq showed the installed copies IDENTICAL to skills/skripsi-skill.
judge_limits: Verdicts for the 111 records that were not re-run come from three Sonnet-medium judge subagents, blind to the old verdicts. Their file reader truncated outputs longer than about 3,300-3,800 characters, so some PASS verdicts rest on partial text, and most PASS reasons are generic.

The 19 re-run verdicts (13 targeted re-runs, 4 clean re-runs after contamination, 2 re-runs of records without a skill read) were judged by the coordinating agent after reading the full observed_output. That agent also wrote the fixes, so these verdicts are not blind to the intent of the change and have no second rater.

One run per case per revision. Codex output varies between runs: EVAL-020 lost its research question and dependency note between 9ff7cd6 and 58a9d29 without a related skill change, so a PASS is one observation, not a pass rate.
Only eight cases ran on the final SKILL.md (d4c8108); the other 122 final records ran on earlier SKILL.md text.

Both follow-up fixes name the scenarios they target: 58a9d29 lists the six pressure requests behind EVAL-046, 085, 094, 097, 107 and QUAL-11, and the d4c8108 example (removing a variable from an approved title) mirrors EVAL-020. PASS on those cases shows the rule is followed when the scenario is named, not that it transfers to unnamed variants.

scripts/audit_skripsi_live.py checks live-review.json and live/ only; this file was checked by an equivalent consistency pass (record identity, hidden oracle, PASS needs an executed record with a successful SKILL.md read) when it was written.

9ff7cd6.skill: Upgraded skill from d85a01a (9ff7cd6 changed only the runner).

58a9d29.skill: Adds the 'valid under pressure' paragraph, closing note in the user's language, readiness check and tracker columns (affected chapters, priority).
58a9d29.use: Re-runs of the 2 old-PASS regressions, the 5 failures, QUAL-04/11/12 and over-refusal checks EVAL-002/020/023.
